subtitle: Step through 10 turning points across Mesoamerica—from early maize villages, cenotes, glyphs, and zero to Pakal's jade mask, Tikal's pyramids, Pok-ta-Pok, Chichen Itza, and living Maya people today.

milestones.title: First Settled Maize, Bean & Squash Farming Villages
milestones.enquiryQuestion: Which three crops grew together as the Mesoamerican "Three Sisters"?
milestones.imageCaption: Colourful Mesoamerican maize (corn) cobs—the sacred crop at the heart of Maya farming and creation stories.
milestones.catalyst: Across Mesoamerica (southern Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador), early Maya families domesticated wild grass into nutritious maize—growing the "Three Sisters" (maize stalks, climbing beans, and ground-shading squash) together!
milestones.turningPoint: Children helped drop maize and bean seeds into holes poked with fire-hardened wooden digging sticks.
milestones.impact: Reliable maize harvests fed settled villages and inspired the Popol Vuh belief that the gods shaped human beings from maize dough!
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. 600 BC): Sacred Cenote Wells, Plastered Reservoirs & Obsidian Trade.

ks2.childrenLife: Children helped drop maize and bean seeds into holes poked with fire-hardened wooden digging sticks.
ks2.quote: “Maize stalks held up climbing bean vines while broad squash leaves shaded the soil damp and weed-free!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: Which three crops grew together as the Mesoamerican "Three Sisters"?

milestones.title: Sacred Cenote Wells, Plastered Reservoirs & Obsidian Trade
milestones.enquiryQuestion: How did Maya cities in the southern Petén jungle store drinking water through the long dry season?
milestones.imageCaption: The deep limestone Sacred Cenote sinkhole at Chichén Itzá in northern Yucatán, Mexico.
milestones.catalyst: To survive dry months with few surface rivers, northern Yucatán towns clustered beside natural limestone sinkholes (cenotes), while southern jungle cities sloped plastered plazas to channel monsoon rain into giant stone reservoirs!
milestones.turningPoint: Families carried clay water jars up stone steps from cool cenotes and watched porters arrive carrying obsidian blades on forehead straps.
milestones.impact: Water engineering plus trade in sharp volcanic obsidian, jade, salt, and quetzal feathers allowed huge stone cities to rise.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. 300 BC – AD 350): Maya Hieroglyphs & Independent Invention of Number Zero!.

ks2.childrenLife: Families carried clay water jars up stone steps from cool cenotes and watched porters arrive carrying obsidian blades on forehead straps.
ks2.quote: “Volcanic obsidian glass from highland Guatemala flaked into cutting edges sharper than modern steel scalpels!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: How did Maya cities in the southern Petén jungle store drinking water through the long dry season?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: They paved wide plazas with waterproof lime stucco angled gently so heavy rainy-season storms drained into deep stone reservoirs!

milestones.title: Maya Hieroglyphs & Independent Invention of Number Zero!
milestones.enquiryQuestion: In Maya base-20 mathematics, what number values did a shell, a single dot, and a horizontal bar stand for?
milestones.imageCaption: Finely carved limestone Maya hieroglyphic blocks combining whole-word signs and phonetic syllables at Palenque.
milestones.catalyst: Maya scribes (aj tz’ib) developed over 800 hieroglyphic signs and—centuries before zero reached Europe!—invented a shell symbol for ZERO alongside dots (1) and bars (5) stacked vertically in base-20 place value.
milestones.turningPoint: Young trainee scribes practised counting in twenties (using all 10 fingers and 10 toes!) with shells, pebbles, and twigs.
milestones.impact: While Romans in Britain used numerals with no zero at all, Maya mathematicians calculated Long Count calendar dates spanning millions of years!
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (AD 615–683): K’inich Janaab’ Pakal Rules Palenque & Jade Death Mask.

ks2.story: Maya scribes (aj tz’ib) developed over 800 hieroglyphic signs and—centuries before zero reached Europe!—invented a shell symbol for ZERO alongside dots (1) and bars (5) stacked vertically in base-20 place value.

ks2.childrenLife: Young trainee scribes practised counting in twenties (using all 10 fingers and 10 toes!) with shells, pebbles, and twigs.
ks2.quote: “Only two ancient civilisations in history invented true place-value zero completely independently: India and the Maya!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: In Maya base-20 mathematics, what number values did a shell, a single dot, and a horizontal bar stand for?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: A shell stood for 0, a dot stood for 1, and a bar stood for 5!

milestones.title: K’inich Janaab’ Pakal Rules Palenque & Jade Death Mask
milestones.enquiryQuestion: How old was K’inich Janaab’ Pakal when he became ruler of Palenque, and how long did he reign?
milestones.imageCaption: Mosaic green jade funerary mask of King K’inich Janaab’ Pakal ("Pakal the Great") with shell and obsidian eyes.
milestones.provenance: National Museum of Anthropology, Mexico City / CC BY-SA (Wikimedia Commons)
milestones.catalyst: Taking the throne of Palenque aged just twelve in AD 615 alongside his mother Lady Sak K’uk’, Pakal the Great ruled for 68 years—raising palaces and the Temple of the Inscriptions, where his secret stone crypt and green jade mask were uncovered in 1952!
milestones.turningPoint: Crowned at twelve, young Pakal watched masons carve corbelled stone arches and paint bright red stucco across Palenque’s temples!
milestones.impact: Shows that Classic Maya lands were NOT one single empire, but dozens of rival city-states ruled by holy lords (k’uhul ajaw) and powerful queens like Lady Six Sky.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. AD 700–740): 70-Metre Step-Pyramids & White Sacbe Roads at Tikal.

ks2.childrenLife: Crowned at twelve, young Pakal watched masons carve corbelled stone arches and paint bright red stucco across Palenque’s temples!
ks2.quote: “More precious to the Maya than gold, shimmering green jade symbolised maize shoots, life-breath, and eternity!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: How old was K’inich Janaab’ Pakal when he became ruler of Palenque, and how long did he reign?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: He became king aged just 12 in AD 615 and ruled for 68 years until AD 683!

milestones.title: 70-Metre Step-Pyramids & White Sacbe Roads at Tikal
milestones.enquiryQuestion: What were gleaming white lime-plastered Maya roadways called, and why were they raised above the forest floor?
milestones.imageCaption: Temple I (Temple of the Great Jaguar) rising steeply above the Great Plaza at Tikal in Guatemala.
milestones.catalyst: At its Classic height while Anglo-Saxon kingdoms ruled Britain, Tikal held over 60,000 people! Without metal tools, wheeled carts, or horses, Maya stoneworkers raised pyramids up to 70 metres high topped with carved roof combs and linked plazas via white sacbe roads.
milestones.turningPoint: Walking along raised white lime-plaster sacbe causeways at dusk, families saw the road glow softly in moonlight above muddy jungle ground!
milestones.impact: Proves human engineering, levers, ropes, and soft-then-hardening quarry limestone built cities rivalling anywhere in the medieval world.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. AD 750): Bouncing Rubber Balls & The Sacred Pok-ta-Pok Ballgame.

ks2.story: At its Classic height while Anglo-Saxon kingdoms ruled Britain, Tikal held over 60,000 people! Without metal tools, wheeled carts, or horses, Maya stoneworkers raised pyramids up to 70 metres high topped with carved roof combs and linked plazas via white sacbe roads.
ks2.significance: Proves human engineering, levers, ropes, and soft-then-hardening quarry limestone built cities rivalling anywhere in the medieval world.
ks2.childrenLife: Walking along raised white lime-plaster sacbe causeways at dusk, families saw the road glow softly in moonlight above muddy jungle ground!
ks2.quote: “Every single limestone block at Tikal was quarried with stone tools and hauled by human muscle without wheels or horses!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: What were gleaming white lime-plastered Maya roadways called, and why were they raised above the forest floor?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: Sacbeob (singular: sacbe, meaning "white road")—raised so travellers and processions stayed dry above seasonal mud and swamps!

milestones.title: Bouncing Rubber Balls & The Sacred Pok-ta-Pok Ballgame
milestones.enquiryQuestion: Which parts of their bodies were Pok-ta-Pok ballplayers allowed to use to strike the heavy solid rubber ball?
milestones.imageCaption: Carved feathered-serpent stone scoring ring set high into the wall of the Great Ballcourt at Chichén Itzá.
milestones.catalyst: Three thousand years before modern factories, Mesoamerican makers mixed rubber-tree sap with morning-glory vine juice to create heavy bouncing rubber balls! Wearing thick leather hip-pads inside I-shaped stone courts, players bounced the ball without hands or feet.
milestones.turningPoint: Cheering crowds lined stone ballcourt benches—and gasped whenever a player knocked the heavy ball clean through the high stone ring!
milestones.impact: Echoed the Popol Vuh Hero Twins defeating the Lords of Xibalba (the Underworld) so sun and maize could rise again.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. AD 780): Valuable Cacao Beans, Spicy Chocolate & Maize Tortillas.

ks2.childrenLife: Cheering crowds lined stone ballcourt benches—and gasped whenever a player knocked the heavy ball clean through the high stone ring!
ks2.quote: “When 16th-century Spanish visitors first saw Maya rubber balls bounce high in the air, Europeans thought they were bewitched!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: Which parts of their bodies were Pok-ta-Pok ballplayers allowed to use to strike the heavy solid rubber ball?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: Padded hips, thighs, knees, and elbows—never throwing or kicking with open hands or feet!

milestones.title: Valuable Cacao Beans, Spicy Chocolate & Maize Tortillas
milestones.enquiryQuestion: How did Ancient Maya chocolate drinks taste different from modern sweet milk chocolate bars?
milestones.imageCaption: Ripe Mesoamerican cacao pods and cacao beans—used by the Maya both as marketplace currency and frothy royal drinks.
milestones.catalyst: In thatched family compounds, cooks soaked maize in lime-water to grind tortillas and tamales on volcanic stone metates, tended stingless honeybees, and traded cacao beans like coins—while nobles poured frothy, chilli-spiced chocolate (xocolatl) between tall vases!
milestones.turningPoint: Children helped grind soft nixtamal corn dough on three-legged stone metates and watched weavers tie colourful cotton backstrap looms to shade trees.
milestones.impact: Maya farmers gifted the entire modern world chocolate (cacao), maize, avocados, tomatoes, vanilla, chillies, and squash!
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. AD 800–950): Why Did Southern Rainforest Cities Like Tikal Empty Around AD 900?.

ks2.significance: Maya farmers gifted the entire modern world chocolate (cacao), maize, avocados, tomatoes, vanilla, chillies, and squash!
ks2.childrenLife: Children helped grind soft nixtamal corn dough on three-legged stone metates and watched weavers tie colourful cotton backstrap looms to shade trees.
ks2.quote: “Ten cacao beans could buy a rabbit at market—and clever tricksters sometimes tried painting clay beans to fake money!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: How did Ancient Maya chocolate drinks taste different from modern sweet milk chocolate bars?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: Maya cacao was drunk bitter, frothy, and unsweetened with no cow’s milk or cane sugar—flavoured with chilli pepper, vanilla, or wild honey!

milestones.title: Why Did Southern Rainforest Cities Like Tikal Empty Around AD 900?
milestones.enquiryQuestion: Did ALL Maya people vanish when southern jungle cities like Tikal emptied around AD 900?
milestones.imageCaption: Vivid Classic Maya wall frescoes inside Bonampak showing royal court ceremonies, musicians, and rival city-state warfare.
milestones.catalyst: Between AD 800 and 950, southern cities like Tikal, Palenque, and Copán stopped carving royal stelae and families gradually moved away. Lake-bed mud cores and cave stalagmites reveal severe multi-year droughts struck right alongside deforestation (for lime plaster) and constant city wars!
milestones.turningPoint: As southern city reservoirs dried up, farming families relocated north toward Yucatán groundwater wells and coastal trade routes.
milestones.impact: Busts the old myth of a sudden "mysterious vanishing": multiple environmental and political pressures pushed families toward northern cenotes and coasts.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (c. AD 950–1450): Chichén Itzá’s 365-Step Pyramid, Tulum & The Dresden Codex.

ks2.story: Between AD 800 and 950, southern cities like Tikal, Palenque, and Copán stopped carving royal stelae and families gradually moved away. Lake-bed mud cores and cave stalagmites reveal severe multi-year droughts struck right alongside deforestation (for lime plaster) and constant city wars!
ks2.significance: Busts the old myth of a sudden "mysterious vanishing": multiple environmental and political pressures pushed families toward northern cenotes and coasts.
ks2.childrenLife: As southern city reservoirs dried up, farming families relocated north toward Yucatán groundwater wells and coastal trade routes.
ks2.quote: “Burning twenty trees just to make one square metre of white temple stucco stripped hillsides and worsened local droughts!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: Did ALL Maya people vanish when southern jungle cities like Tikal emptied around AD 900?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: No! Only the crowded southern lowland kingdoms declined—northern Yucatán cities and coastal ports boomed for 600 more years, and millions of Maya live today!

milestones.title: Chichén Itzá’s 365-Step Pyramid, Tulum & The Dresden Codex
milestones.enquiryQuestion: How many surviving ancient Maya bark-paper books (codices) escaped destruction in the 16th century?
milestones.imageCaption: El Castillo pyramid at Chichén Itzá casting seven sunlit triangles down the balustrade onto Kukulcán’s stone serpent head at the equinox.
milestones.catalyst: Northern cities like Chichén Itzá, Uxmal, Mayapán, and cliffside sea-trading Tulum thrived for centuries! Builders designed El Castillo with exactly 365 steps casting Kukulcán’s equinox serpent shadow beside El Caracol observatory, while scribes painted the surviving Dresden Codex.
milestones.turningPoint: At spring and autumn equinox sunsets, crowds watched seven triangles of sunlight slither down El Castillo’s staircase like a living snake!
milestones.impact: Even though Spanish Bishop Diego de Landa burned Maya bark books in AD 1562, four precious codices survived—and Landa’s own notes later helped Yuri Knorozov decode Maya glyphs!
milestones.bridgeToNext: Next turning point (Today (21st Century)): Over 7 Million Living Maya People Today & Airborne LiDAR Discoveries.

ks2.quote: “Four staircases of 91 steps (364) plus the top temple platform (1) equalled the 365 days of the Haab’ solar year!”
ks2.detectiveQuestion: How many surviving ancient Maya bark-paper books (codices) escaped destruction in the 16th century?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: Only four authentic Maya codices survive today (the Dresden, Madrid, Paris, and Maya of Mexico/Grolier codices)!

milestones.title: Over 7 Million Living Maya People Today & Airborne LiDAR Discoveries
milestones.enquiryQuestion: How does modern airborne LiDAR technology find Maya cities without chopping down a single rainforest tree?
milestones.imageCaption: A contemporary Maya weaver in Guatemala crafting intricate geometric textiles on a traditional backstrap loom.
milestones.catalyst: Today over seven million Maya people live across Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador—speaking around 30 Mayan languages, weaving dazzling huipils, and farming maize—while planes firing harmless LiDAR laser pulses peel back tree canopies to map 60,000+ hidden ancient structures!
milestones.turningPoint: Modern Maya schoolchildren learn both Spanish and Mayan languages like Yucatec, K’iche’, and Kaqchikel—and new Maya epigraphers read their ancestors’ stone stelae!
milestones.impact: Proves Maya civilisation is both an extraordinary ancient story and a vibrant living heritage right now.
milestones.bridgeToNext: Completes all 10 turning points in The Ancient Maya (c. 2000 BC–Today).

ks2.detectiveQuestion: How does modern airborne LiDAR technology find Maya cities without chopping down a single rainforest tree?
ks2.detectiveAnswer: Planes bounce millions of harmless laser light pulses through tiny gaps in the leaves to map the exact 3D shape of stone ruins on the forest floor!
